title: Smooth Cruiser at Lyft: Built for Safety and Transparency
summary: At Lyft, we want to ensure everyone on the Lyft platform is supported by smart, fair tools to improve their experience. This is the guiding principle behind Smooth Cruiser, our feature that provides Drivers with insights into their driving behavior. For a tool like this to truly help Drivers make informed decisions…

title: Agents are users, so your software needs evals
summary: Agents are now users of software, doing work on people's behalf. Whether you're building the agent or the software it uses (API, CLI, MCP server, SDK), evals give you a way to measure how well that work gets done.

title: Launching the Vite Ecosystem Fund
summary: Cloudflare is distributing the first $301,300 of the Vite Ecosystem Fund to open source projects and maintainers. The recipients were chosen by a panel of Vite stack core team members, including maintainers not employed by Cloudflare.

title: Beyond API Compatibility: Building a Tool to Measure the Blast Radius of Library Changes
summary: At Netflix, shared Java libraries support applications developed across a large, independently evolving repository ecosystem. A library change begins in one repository, but its impact can reach many others. Producers can see the API diff in front of them. What they often cannot see is who still depends on the symbols…

title: Origin Range Requests: Serving large files without range-request tuning
summary: Naive byte-range caching can waste gigabytes of origin bandwidth on small requests. We rebuilt our cache architecture in Pingora to coordinate partial fetches automatically, cutting R2 p99 latency in half.

title: Bringing post-quantum cryptography to geographically fenced key management
summary: Cloudflare's new post-quantum GeoKey Manager protects geographically fenced decryption keys from harvest now, decrypt later attacks. Learn how we redesigned our cryptography stack to support strict data sovereignty in a post-quantum world.

title: 4 real? Tracking exploitation and patching of eMudhra’s weak keys
summary: Four, just four: that’s the key to break into any unpatched connection on the Internet that is using eMudhra certificates. Here’s how we quickly patched Cloudflare, what evidence we can see of attempted exploitation, and how much of the rest of the Internet remains exposed.

title: Cloudflare services for private origins is now generally available
summary: Public traffic to private origins, with WAF, bot management, caching, and Workers, is now available to every customer with Cloudflare One connectivity.

title: Introducing Geist Serif
summary: Geist started as a monospace typeface for developers, built for the editors and terminals where they spend their day doing their work. From there it grew into Geist Sans for product interfaces, and then into Geist Pixel, which was inspired by the grids of early computer screens.

title: Simplifying runtime caching on Vercel
summary: Today, we’re bringing Data Cache into Runtime Cache, giving developers one product for data caching across frameworks and APIs. If you use Next.js fetch caching or unstable_cache , you won’t need to change your code. Pro and Enterprise projects will get larger storage allocations.

title: Beyond code generation: A developer’s guide to agentic engineering
summary: Writing code got faster. The work around it didn't. See how you can plan, write code, review changes, and investigate production issues with GitHub Copilot, and what work still needs your judgment.

title: Introducing Vercel Schedules
summary: Cron jobs are useful for work that needs to happen regularly. You can use them to do things such as back up your database on a schedule, or keep data in sync between two systems.

title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants
summary: Cloudflare mitigated over 8,200 DDoS attacks per hour in Q3 2026 as attackers shifted to shorter, high-frequency strikes. Explore the latest threat data, including the collapse of CLDAP vectors and the impact of recent botnet takedowns.

title: Introducing the Cloudflare PHP Capture the Flag challenge
summary: We are launching a PHP Capture the Flag challenge integrated with our Bug Bounty program to test our WAF protections. Security researchers are invited to bypass our defenses and capture the flag to help make the Internet safer.

title: What took the Internet offline in Q3 2026
summary: An examination of global Internet disruptions observed by Cloudflare Radar during the third quarter of 2026. This review analyzes how power failures, natural disasters, and government shutdowns impacted network connectivity and traffic.

title: Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model, and our remediation with SGLang
summary: A configuration mismatch in GLM 5.3 on Workers AI triggered an SGLang bug that exposed KV cache pages across requests. Here is how we addressed the issue.

title: Kitesurf is now open source
summary: Kitesurf, our experimental browser engine for AI agents, is now open source. Inspect the code, run it locally, or deploy your own instance on Cloudflare Workers.

title: Adapting to AI penetration testing orchestrators: The Modern Security Model
summary: AI-orchestrated penetration testing platforms like ARTEX have become increasingly powerful tools enabling effective attacks on exposed infrastructure. Here we share Cloudflare’s observations and recommended countermeasures.

title: Workflow SDK 5: built for production
summary: When we first launched Workflow SDK, the goal was simple: write regular async JavaScript, and let the SDK keep it running through crashes, deployments, and long waits.

title: The post-quantum future of web privacy
summary: Cryptographic protocols like Privacy Pass help keep web sites safe from abuse while keeping their users private. This post looks at the quantum threat to these protocols, and some new post-quantum cryptography that may help close the gap.

title: Inside GitHub’s new Git storage architecture
summary: GitHub's new Git storage architecture is built so thousands of agents can push to a single repository at once. Here's how it works.

title: Agents aren’t humans (but they kinda are)
summary: AI agents act for millions, but servers see intermediaries that strip user visibility. This post defines the problem space and introduces a collaborative approach to safely identifying, allowing, and managing this automated traffic.

title: Introducing Spend Management: Spending limits and alerts for Cloudflare
summary: Spend Management adds opt-in spending caps for Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects, and more products soon. Here is how we built the metering pipeline that turns usage into runtime decisions.

title: Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills
summary: Agent skills capture repeatable engineering work in files teams can review and reuse, while tools, project context, and permissions remain specific to the host that runs them.

title: How two engineer side projects became the agent taking action inside Dropbox
summary: Two side projects explored a new way to get work done with files already in Dropbox. Here’s how engineers brought them together and turned those experiments into a new customer experience.

title: How AI-assisted development helped us build the new Dropbox experience
summary: From sharing features across web and desktop to testing the details customers depend on, this is how AI-assisted development helped our engineers deliver the updated Dropbox experience.

title: Introducing Virtual Models on AI Gateway
summary: Virtual Models are an abstraction of the model string and configurations your apps and developers use. With a single virtual model ID, you can change and update models, configure fallbacks and priority, and enforce Zero Data Retention centrally. The virtual model configuration applies wherever the ID is used.

title: Introducing Vercel CI
summary: Coding agents are opening more pull requests than ever, and each one waits on CI before anyone can review or merge it. Most CI systems run the entire workflow on every push, even a one-line change. The more your agents push, the more time you spend waiting on CI.

title: Choosing QuePaxa, an unusual consensus algorithm
summary: Cloudflare is building an experimental consensus service using a never-before-deployed consensus algorithm, QuePaxa. In this post we explain how QuePaxa works and why we chose it.

title: See the agents, set the terms: New visibility and control for personal agents
summary: Personal AI agents have changed how users interact with the web, blurring the lines between automated and human traffic. Learn how Cloudflare gives site owners visibility and control to manage personal agent access.

title: Introducing Zero Wire, a hub for investigating critical Internet vulnerabilities
summary: Zero Wire on Cloudflare Radar pairs plain-language briefings with global attack telemetry and remediation steps. Triage critical CVEs faster and decide how to protect your infrastructure.

summary: Interactive partner demos in under two hours with v0, replacing a process that could take weeks

title: Beyond Test Cards: A Fake Payment Provider for Testing at Scale
summary: Lyft processes billions in payments annually, and that volume continues to grow. Agentic coding has drastically accelerated feature development, but it raises the stakes for the one phase that cannot be rushed: ensuring the highest standards of reliability and correctness in critical payment systems.
